title: Anatomical terminology: position, planes, directions and movement
description: Learn anatomical position, sagittal, coronal and transverse planes, directional terms and joint movements using an honest conceptual body model.

questions.question: What is the standard anatomical position?
questions.answer: The subject stands upright facing forward, with arms at the sides and palms facing anteriorly; thumbs point laterally. Right and left always belong to the subject, even when a patient is lying down.

questions.question: How do sagittal, coronal and transverse planes differ?
questions.answer: A sagittal plane separates right from left, a coronal plane separates anterior from posterior, and a transverse plane separates superior from inferior. The median sagittal plane passes through the midline.

questions.question: What is the difference between proximal and distal?
questions.answer: Proximal means closer to the point where a limb joins the trunk; distal means farther from that attachment. The elbow is proximal to the wrist in the upper limb.

questions.question: Why does patient right appear on the left side of a front-facing illustration?
questions.answer: An anterior image faces the patient. Their right side is therefore on the observer’s left. Anatomical descriptions use the patient’s own side, not the screen’s left or right.

questions.question: Are the colored planes in this atlas real body membranes?
questions.answer: No. The translucent sheets are computer-generated reference planes used to explain sections. They are not physical tissues, and the chapter does not place false anatomical pins on them.
